gate.reason: Two human calls, neither of them authority — `architecture.md` puts the module list in the tree's hands, so plan does not need a Decision to name `src/lock.rs`. (1) Sequencing and cost: a behavior-neutral ~2060-line move whose fence spans 59 files (16 `src/`, 42 `tests/it/`, plus `drift.rs`) can share a wave with nothing, so it runs alone against a drained queue and buys churn against no test that could go red — whether to buy it at all is the human's. (2) Where the row→model lifts land (`requirement_from_row` 6248, `clause_from_row` 6276, `edges_from_declarations` 6293, `mention_edges_from_declarations` 6333): recommended answer is beside the model type they produce — `compose`/`graph`, which is where `compose::clause_from_row` (407) already lives and what `drift::clause_from_row`'s thin delegation to it already implies — leaving `lock.rs` a codec with no model dependency. A ruling the other way (the lifts ride the codec) is one word in this entry.

new.description: The flat module (`architecture.md`, "The tree stays flat": a split lands as a new flat module) owning the lock declaration codec moved verbatim from `src/drift.rs` 4298-6360 — `Declarations` and every `*Row` type, their `*_table`/`*_from_table` TOML round-trip pairs, the column readers, `LockRowError`/`RowError`, and the read/parse door (`read_lock_document`, `read_declarations`, `read_engine`, `parse_declarations`, `declarations_from_doc`). A pure move: no signature, no behavior, no row column changes, and `drift` imports it rather than re-exporting it — one door per name, never two (`engineering.md`, "An export earns its consumer").

summary: src/drift.rs carries three jobs in 6703 lines; the lock declaration codec (~2060 of them) splits to a flat src/lock.rs, drift keeping emit + place

tests.asserts: the codec's own round-trip suite passes unchanged against `src/lock.rs` — the move's one proof, since nothing here is a behavior claim
the ts-rs export byte-compare stays green with `sdk/src/generated/**` untouched — the bindings are keyed by type name, not module path, so the move stops at the Rust side

acceptance: cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --all --check and the rustdoc gate green; `src/lock.rs` owns the declaration codec, `src/drift.rs`'s header describes everything the file still holds, no consumer reaches a codec symbol through `drift`, and `git diff --stat` shows `sdk/src/generated/` unchanged.
